title: Aurora Health - Redwood Onboarding Kickoff
next_steps: Send onboarding playbook and architecture guide (Samir)
Provision Redwood Console access and SSO invite (Jenna)
action_items: Samir Patel: Share pricing/commit options by 2026-12-20
Liam Chen: Schedule private deployment readiness call and request network diagrams by 2026-12-22
Maya Thompson: Confirm list of pilot use cases by 2026-12-21
Jenna Morales: Set up Aurora's Redwood Console access and SSO onboarding by 2026-12-23
summary: Kickoff for Aurora Health onboarding to Redwood. Covered high-level architecture choices (hosted vs dedicated vs private), security/compliance requirements (SSO, audit logs, KMS), pilot scope (chat + embeddings), timelines, and next steps. Action items assigned.
transcript:
[00:00] Samir Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Samir from Redwood, AE on the account. Quick roll call? 
[00:07] Maya Thompson: Maya here, Director of Engineering at Aurora. 
[00:10] Ethan Brooks: Ethan, VP Product. 
[00:13] Sofia Martinez: Sofia, IT Security. 
[00:15] Oliver Reed: Oliver, DevOps. 
[00:18] Jenna Morales: Jenna, Customer Success at Redwood. 
[00:21] Liam Chen: Liam, Solutions Engineer. 
[00:24] Samir Patel: Great. Agenda  - intro, current stack, security reqs, pilot scope, timeline, next steps. Quick context from you Maya on what success looks like? 
[00:35] Maya Thompson: Sure, so for Aurora success is twofold, one get chat features into our patient portal with sub-200ms latency on common flows and two have embeddings for triage and search. We need to keep PHI off hosted env unless encrypted with customer keys, so privacy is huge. 
[00:52] Samir Patel: Got it. Quick qual questions - current infra? 
[00:55] Oliver Reed: We're on GCP, k8s for app, we use a managed Postgres, and current ML infra is a mix  - some hosted LLMs and an in-house vector store. We prefer VPC peering for dedicated/ private deployments. 
[01:10] Liam Chen: Thanks, Oliver. On the infra side, Redwood can support hosted API for fast ramp, Dedicated reserved pools for predictable throughput and a Private deployment (VPC) if you need customer-managed networking and KMS. 
[01:25] Sofia Martinez: Regarding KMS, we need HSM-backed keys and audit logging, SOC 2 type II, and data retention rules for 7 years. Also SSO with SAML and RBAC. Do you support SAML? 
[01:36] Jenna Morales: Yes we support SAML SSO, role-based access, and we can integrate with your KMS. For audit logs, we can retain events and we have enterprise packages for longer retention. I'll share the security binder. 
[01:48] Ethan Brooks: On pricing, what's the delta between hosted vs dedicated? We're trying to understand unit cost vs SLA. 
[01:55] Samir Patel: Hosted is usage-based, lower commitment, higher per-token unit cost compared to Dedicated reserved capacity which has better unit economics for steady usage. We can share a cost model; I'll send a sample worksheet. 
[02:10] Maya Thompson: For the pilot we want to start with chat in the portal for triage and a embeddings index for provider search. Timeline: pilot in Jan, go-live with MVP in Mar. 
[02:22] Liam Chen: For the pilot we recommend doing a hosted -> dedicated migration plan, or directly start with Dedicated if you're confident on traffic. Also we can run benchmarks; can you share representative prompts and sequence lengths? 
[02:35] Oliver Reed: Yeah we'll compile those. Also network constraints  - we need private peering and egress rules documentation. 
[02:40] Sofia Martinez: We'll need a security review; can we schedule a deep dive with your security team? 
[02:43] Jenna Morales: Absolutely, Liam can lead a security deep-dive. We'll send the SSO SAML docs and security binder. 
[02:50] Samir Patel: OK let's recap next steps. I'll send pricing and onboarding playbook. Liam to schedule private deploy readiness call and request network diagrams. Jenna to provision console access and invite for SSO setup. Maya to confirm pilot use cases. 
[03:05] Ethan Brooks: Sounds good. Any competitors you're aware of? We evaluated Anthropic and an internal build. 
[03:10] Samir Patel: Noted. Also quick question on data residency  - are you required to keep data in-region? 
[03:15] Maya Thompson: Yes, US-only for patient data. 
[03:18] Liam Chen: We can pin deployments to US regions and provide VPC options. 
[03:22] Oliver Reed: On integration  - we plan to call the API from our backend and use prefix caching for common prompts. 
[03:28] Liam Chen: Great, caching and batching will help with cost. We'll provide recommendations on batching / quantization for embeddings. 
[03:35] Sofia Martinez: One more security ask  - can you support certificate pinning and IP allowlists? 
[03:39] Jenna Morales: Yes, IP allowlists and mTLS options exist for Dedicated/Private. I'll include detail in the binder. 
[03:46] Samir Patel: Timeline recap - send docs by end of week, security deep-dive next week, pilot kickoff in early Jan. 
[03:53] Maya Thompson: Thanks everyone. 
[03:55] Samir Patel: Thanks, we'll follow up with action items. Bye.
